props.segment: Trust the Direction, Distrust the Decimals
props.command: Can I trust Kimi K3's benchmark table?
props.runningText: reading the technical report and adversarial audit…
output: The coarse claim holds — best open model, corroborated by three independent evaluators.
The decimals don't — harness advantage, no error bars, modified benchmarks.
Trust the direction. Distrust the decimals.

beats.narration_text: Can I trust Kimi K3's benchmark table? That's the question. The coarse answer: yes — the best open model claim is corroborated by three independent evaluators. The fine-grained answer: no — the sub-point rankings are not supported by the evidence. Here's the skeptical read.

props.title: Kimi K3 — Trust the Direction, Distrust the Decimals

props.headline: Kimi K3 — What It Is
props.body: An open-weight frontier model from Moonshot AI. 2.8 trillion parameters, July 2026, the strongest open model that exists. Open-weights matter because they define who can run frontier AI. The headline claim: 2.5× better training efficiency over K2. Both claims need careful reading — here's what holds and what doesn't.

beats.narration_text: Kimi K3 is Moonshot's open-weight frontier model — 2.8 trillion parameters, released July 2026. Open weights matter because they determine who controls frontier AI infrastructure. Moonshot claims 2.5× better training efficiency. Both the ranking and the efficiency claim need reading. That's what this is.

shot.visual_intent: FormACard light. The one-sentence claim printed as a serif quote block. Karaoke reveal: claim appears, then the conditional follows.

props.headline: The one-sentence thesis
props.body: Kimi K3 achieves frontier performance — the strongest open model, trailing only Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. If that ranking is an artifact of evaluation setup rather than model quality, the whole report's thesis collapses.

beats.narration_text: One sentence: Kimi K3 is the best open model available, trailing only Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol. The entire report rests on that. If the ranking is an artifact of evaluation setup rather than model quality — the thesis collapses.

shot.visual_intent: Manim B04_RankingChart: three independent evaluator bars. K3 gold. Source labels for each. No Kimi harness.

graphic.mechanic: Three-panel horizontal rank display. Panel 1: Artificial Analysis Elo bar (K3=1547, labeled '#4 of 580'). Panel 2: Vals AI rank bar (K3 #2 of 39 frontier models). Panel 3: LMArena WebDev Arena (K3 labeled '#1 open model'). All K3 bars gold. Source tag bottom each panel. Animate panels left-to-right, each appears on narration cue.

beats.narration_text: Three independent evaluators — no Kimi harness. Artificial Analysis ranks K3 fourth of 580 models, Elo 1547. Vals AI puts it second of 39 frontier models. LMArena WebDev Arena: the first open model to ever top the leaderboard. That coarse signal is trustworthy.

shot.credit: Kimi K3 blog / Moonshot AI — vendor chart, citation use

beats.narration_text: The size chart makes it concrete: as of July 2026, K3 is the largest open model by total parameters. That milestone is real and independently confirmed.

shot.visual_intent: FormACard Form B. Three spec items with simple line icons, karaoke reveal.

beats.narration_text: The architecture is Mixture-of-Experts: 2.8 trillion total parameters, but only 104 billion activate per token. 16 experts selected out of 896. A sparsely activated giant with a 1-million-token context.

shot.visual_intent: Manim B08_MoEGrid: 896 squares grid (e.g. 32×28), 16 lit gold on each 'token tick'. Activation fraction label.

graphic.mechanic: Grid of 896 small squares arranged 32×28. On each 'token tick' (every 1.5s), 16 random squares pulse gold, all others dim grey. Label top: '16 / 896 experts'. Label bottom: '1.8% activation'. Animate three ticks — different 16 each time to show sparsity.

beats.narration_text: Each token routes to 16 experts out of 896. Most of the model stays dark. The sparsity is how you build a 2.8-trillion-parameter model that's still practically runnable on real hardware.

shot.credit: Moonshot AI / Kimi K3 promotional video — vendor footage, citation use

beats.narration_text: Moonshot's marketing is not shy. 'Designed a chip for its nano self.' The gap between that voice and the technical fine print is exactly the territory we're navigating.

shot.visual_intent: FormACard A light. Claim stated as serif text block. 'approximately 2.5×' in terracotta.

props.headline: The scaling efficiency claim
props.body: The architectural redesign from K2 to K3 delivers approximately 2.5× better scaling efficiency — meaning K3 reaches the same validation loss using 2.5 times fewer training FLOPs.

beats.narration_text: The secondary load-bearing claim: the redesign from K2 to K3 delivers approximately 2.5× better scaling efficiency. For the same validation loss, K3 needs 2.5 times fewer compute FLOPs. Figure 7 shows this.

shot.visual_intent: Manim B12_IsoLossCurves: Fig. 7 iso-loss scaling law. K2 dim blue, K3 gold, iso-gap arrow terracotta. --verify block in scenes.py.

graphic.mechanic: Log-scale FLOP axis (x, 10^22 to 10^25). Validation loss axis (y). K2 curve draws first (dim blue), then K3 curve appears (gold, shifted LEFT by log10(2.5) ≈ 0.4 decades). At a fixed loss level, a horizontal dashed terracotta line spans the gap. Animated label: '~2.5× fewer FLOPs for same loss'. Curves use power-law decay: loss = A + B * (FLOPs)^(-alpha). K2 and K3 share A, B, alpha; K3 FLOPs multiplied by 2.5 (i.e. K3 x-coord = K2 x-coord / 2.5).

beats.narration_text: Figure 7: two scaling laws. K2 and K3. At any fixed validation loss, K3 reaches it using 2.5 times fewer training FLOPs. That horizontal gap is the efficiency claim — and it's plotted on Moonshot's own out-of-distribution validation set.

shot.visual_intent: FormACard A light. Four bundled components listed, terracotta arrow pointing down to '= one curve'. No ablation note.

props.headline: The bundle problem
props.body: That 2.5× curve bundles four changes at once: KDA (new attention type) · Attention Residuals · Stable LatentMoE · new data recipe. No ablation separates them. The curve says 'all four together work.' It says nothing about which one matters most.

beats.narration_text: The problem: that curve bundles four changes at once. KDA. Attention Residuals. Stable LatentMoE. A new data recipe. No ablation separates them. 'The whole redesign is 2.5× more efficient' is all it supports — nothing more.

shot.visual_intent: Architecture diagram screenshot showing Stable LatentMoE, KDA, Gated MLA, AttnRes blocks. Terracotta drawon rings on each of the four component labels in sequence.
shot.credit: Kimi K3 technical report / Moonshot AI — architecture diagram, citation use

beats.narration_text: The architecture diagram names all four. Each gets its own box — Stable LatentMoE, KDA, Gated MLA, Attention Residuals. All four shipped together. You cannot read the efficiency curve as evidence for any single one.

shot.visual_intent: Manim B16_GPQAChart: 6-bar horizontal chart GPQA Diamond. K3 gold, others dim. 'no CIs shown' terracotta annotation. GPT-5.6 Sol bar annotated as leading.

graphic.mechanic: Horizontal bar chart, 6 models. K3=93.5 (gold), Fable5=92.6 (dim, asterisk label 'w/ fallback'), GPT-5.6 Sol=94.1 (dim blue, leading), Opus4.8=91.0 (dim), GPT5.5=93.5 (dim), GLM5.2=91.2 (dim). Bars animate in. Terracotta text annotation appears: 'no confidence intervals shown'. Terracotta gap bracket: 'K3 vs Sol: 0.6 pts'.

beats.narration_text: GPQA Diamond: doctoral-level science questions. K3 scores 93.5. GPT-5.6 Sol scores 94.1. The difference is 0.6 points. No error bars anywhere in Table 2. That 0.6 might be sampling noise.

shot.visual_intent: FormACard A light. 'No Error Bars' as headline. Body explains the evidential problem.

props.headline: No error bars
props.body: Single point estimates. Temperature 1.0. No confidence intervals, no standard deviations, no seed counts — except on a handful of vision benchmarks that explicitly report three runs. The headline Table 2 presents sub-point differences as findings.

beats.narration_text: Single point estimates, temperature 1.0, no confidence intervals, no seed counts. The only exceptions are a few vision benchmarks averaging three runs. The headline table presents sub-point differences as findings — they're not.

shot.visual_intent: Manim B18_SWEMarathonChart: 6-bar SWE-Marathon. K3 leads but Fable5 has fallback annotation.

graphic.mechanic: Horizontal bar chart, 6 models. K3=42.0 (gold, leading), Fable5=35.0 (dim, red asterisk '35% fallback rate'), GPT-5.6 Sol=39.0 (dim), Opus4.8=40.0 (dim), GPT5.5=14.0 (dim), GLM5.2=13.0 (dim). Terracotta bracket on K3 vs Fable5 gap: 'K3 leads by 7' — then a subscript note 'Fable5: 35% fallback'.

beats.narration_text: SWE-Marathon: one of K3's real leads. 42 to 35 over Fable 5 — seven points. But Fable 5 hit fallbacks on 35% of tasks in this evaluation. The lead is probably real, but the exact gap is inflated.

beats.narration_text: The engineering is real. The promotional materials are polished. The fine print is where things get complicated. Four problems in the evaluation design.

shot.visual_intent: FormACard B light. Problem 1 with house icon. Karaoke: label appears, then explanation.

items.label: Home field advantage
items.sublabel: K3 runs under Kimi Code. Claude models under Claude Code. GPT under Codex. Each model evaluated in its own team's harness.

beats.narration_text: Problem one: home field advantage. Kimi K3 is evaluated under Kimi Code — its own team's harness. Claude models run under Claude Code. GPT under Codex. Each model benefits from tooling its own team built and tuned.

shot.visual_intent: Manim B21_CrossHarnessChart: K3 under own harness vs Claude Code, plus GPT-Sol under Codex. Shows cross-harness gaps are large.

graphic.mechanic: Grouped bar chart, Kimi Code Bench 2.0. Three groups: (1) K3 under Kimi Code (72.9, gold), (2) K3 under Claude Code (73.7, gold-lighter, note: 'K3 actually scores higher here'), (3) GPT-5.6 Sol under Codex (64.8, dim blue), (4) Fable5 under Claude Code (76.9, dim). Terracotta bracket: 'K3 vs Sol sharing Claude Code harness: ~9 pts'. Note: raw numbers from README footnote §2.

beats.narration_text: On Kimi Code Bench 2.0: K3 under its own harness scores 72.9. Under Claude Code, it scores 73.7 — similar. GPT-5.6 Sol under Codex scores 64.8. Cross-harness gaps are large and completely uncontrolled.

shot.visual_intent: FormACard B light. Problem 2 with asterisk/footnote icon.

items.label: Degraded competitors
items.sublabel: Fable 5 results 'include fallback behaviors.' Sol results 'include cyberguards.' Both conditions reduce scores. K3 still loses to both — meaning the real gap is wider, not narrower.

beats.narration_text: Problem two: the two models that beat K3 are shown in a degraded state. Fable 5 results include fallback behaviors. GPT-5.6 Sol results include cyberguards. Both depress the competitor scores. K3 still loses — so the real gap is wider than the table shows.

shot.visual_intent: FormACard B light. Problem 3 with pencil/edit icon.

items.label: Author-modified benchmarks
items.sublabel: SWE-Marathon: H20-calibrated branch. PostTrainBench: H20 instead of H100. FrontierSWE: dominance scores recomputed. Each defensible alone. K3's strongest coding leads ride on non-standard variants.

beats.narration_text: Problem three: author-modified variants. SWE-Marathon recalibrated for H20 hardware. PostTrainBench run on H20 instead of H100. FrontierSWE dominance scores recomputed. Each change is defensible individually. Collectively, K3's best coding numbers ride on non-standard versions.

shot.visual_intent: FormACard B light. Problem 4 with lock icon.

items.label: Internal benchmarks
items.sublabel: Table 3 is in-house, undisclosed, and per §6.2.1 'refreshed frequently to directly guide data and training iterations.' A benchmark you optimize toward is a training signal, not a test.

beats.narration_text: Problem four: internal benchmarks. Table 3 is in-house, undisclosed, and — per the paper's own methods section — refreshed frequently to directly guide training iterations. A benchmark you optimize toward is a training signal, not an independent test.

beats.act: ACT V: ERROR BARS — THE MISSING EVIDENCE
ACT V: ERROR BARS — THE MISSING EVIDENCE

shot.visual_intent: Manim B26_ErrorBarDemo: CorpFin v2 bars, shown first without CI then with ±1.0 bands that cause complete overlap.

graphic.mechanic: Two-phase animation. Phase 1: plain bars, K3=71.6 (gold) vs Fable5=71.8 (dim). Terracotta label: 'Fable 5 leads by 0.2'. Phase 2: ±1.0 error bands grow onto both bars. Bars now completely overlap. Terracotta label changes to: 'Indistinguishable with any realistic CI'. Source: CorpFin v2, Table 2.

beats.narration_text: CorpFin v2: K3 scores 71.6, Fable 5 scores 71.8. Fable 5 leads by 0.2 points. Add any realistic confidence interval — even ±0.5 — and the bars overlap completely. That ranking is not interpretable.

shot.visual_intent: FormACard A light. The defensible narrowed claim, stated clearly in terracotta.

props.headline: The defensible claim
props.body: Kimi K3 is the strongest open-weight model as of July 2026, competitive with second-tier proprietary models (≈ Claude Opus 4.8 / GPT-5.5), clearly behind frontier leaders (Fable 5, GPT-5.6 Sol). Three independent evaluators corroborate this. The specific sub-point wins in Table 2 are within evaluation noise.
props.accent: trust the direction, not the decimals

beats.narration_text: The defensible claim: K3 is the best open model, competitive with second-tier proprietary systems, clearly behind the frontier leaders. Three independent evaluators corroborate exactly that — and nothing more. Trust the direction, not the decimals.

graphic.mechanic: Two-bar chart. K3: 32% (gold bar). US frontier models: 76% (dim blue bar). Both bars animate up. Terracotta annotation below K3 bar: '0 / 41 arbitrary code execution tasks'. beats.narration_text: The UK AISI and US CAISI ran an independent cyber assessment. K3 scored 32%. US frontier models scored 76%. Zero of 41 arbitrary code execution tasks succeeded. Moonshot published this result — that disclosure is genuine honesty.

props.artifactHeading: Trust the Direction, Distrust the Decimals
artifactLines: K3 is real — best open model, corroborated independently.
Home harness. Degraded competitors. Modified benchmarks. No error bars.
2.5× is the whole redesign — not any single component.

beats.narration_text: Trust the direction: Kimi K3 is the strongest open model as of July 2026 — three independent evaluators agree. Distrust the decimals: harness advantage, degraded competitors, modified benchmarks, no error bars. The 2.5× is the whole redesign, not any one component. That's the skeptical read.

output: This is the move the skeptical read teaches.
The footnotes are in the paper — you just have to read them.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Open Table 2 in the K3 report. Find the three benchmarks where K3's lead is largest. For each one, find the harness footnote in §6.1 or §6.2. Ask which leads survive a shared harness. That exercise is the skeptical read in practice — the footnotes are all there.
